rv.q: It is the comeuppance of the arriviste. Brought down to size, he is no less indignant for it. In a smart, unyielding performance, he goes from pompous to bruised – and ever unrepentant.

Viola falls for Orsino, Olivia falls for Viola. In a comedy sub-plot Olivia's drunken uncle Sir Toby Belch, his friend Sir Andrew Aguecheek with her servant Maria scheme to undermine Olivia's pompous steward, Malvolio. The set is a circular stone patio with three stone benches which revolve to create larger seating areas.

We see the narrative emerge through Feste's eyes, who also brings the show to a cyclical end with his song When That I Was and a Little Tiny Boy . Birrell glows with a magnificent voice and spirit, where Feste embodies the topsy-turvy energy of the 'twelfth night' festival with verbal sharpness and riddles.

But with substantially the same cast and a similar staging, it feels like a suitable companion piece. Director Jamie Glover makes his vision of Illyria a special one with a revolving platform keeping the action fluid, while set designer Amanda Stoodley’s minimalist aesthetic makes superb use of the theatre’s thrust stage.

Jordan was brilliant as Malvolio, giving the character an odious, toadying quality in Act 1, which was still present throughout his journey in Act 2. With these choices, it was hard to feel any real sympathy for the character. Jordan stole the stage every time and he was one of the highlights of the show for me.
